why_next: This experiment established behavioral signals as a validated detection dimension (C1-C3 PASS: TP=1.0, FP=0.0, AUC=1.0 on real HTTP Flask+PyJWT) but C4 orthogonality failed (|r|=0.593) due to measurement design flaw: 5/15 co-occurring conditions have zero structural observability because auth-drift (signing_key_rotation) causes HTTP 401 on all endpoints, masking structural signal to imputed 0.0. The orthogonality hypothesis is untested, not falsified. The minimum next step is to fix the co-occurring measurement so both signals are non-trivially observable on the same conditions — either via independent structural probes (unauthenticated endpoint access), baseline-schema comparison independent of auth response, or drift patterns that do not uniformly block all endpoints. If orthogonality survives the fixed design, C-FRESHNESS gains a validated second detection channel. If it fails with proper measurement, behavioral signals are confirmed non-orthogonal and the domain pivots to composite multi-signal classifiers or real-API deployments.

recommended_action: Design a graph lane experiment that fixes the co-occurring drift+noise measurement design: (1) use drift patterns that do NOT uniformly block all endpoints (e.g., permission_boundary + optional_field_addition, session_invalidation + description_change — these already work with non-zero structural observability); (2) add independent structural probe (unauthenticated GET to retrieve response body schema without requiring valid token); (3) or compute structural signal from baseline schema definitions rather than live response bodies; (4) add per-sample stochastic variation that actually varies both signals within conditions (not deterministic fixed pairs). If behavioral vs structural Pearson r < 0.3 on the fixed co-occurring design, C-FRESHNESS gains a validated second detection channel and the product pipeline can integrate behavioral signals. If r >= 0.3 with proper measurement, behavioral signals are confirmed non-orthogonal and the domain pivots to composite multi-signal classifiers or real-API stochastic deployments.
